frog.speaker: D
frog.excerpt: We got up very early and drove to Izmir, where we had breakfast, we are in a campsite. There are free gas rings, so for lunch, nice and clean after a shower, H and I cooked pancakes, they were delicious. In the afternoon we made a tent over the drying racks, with duvets etc. At night we had spaghetti and on the way back from the van, I caught a frog, it was about 1½” long, when not stretched out jumping, it was very slimy and slippery to hold. There were lots of cats as well.

frog.speaker: F
frog.excerpt: We did a three kilometre walk to the shops. It was a windy road near the sea. There were lots of flies. We bought some bread and grapes then we came back. Dad and I did some exploring and found lots of frogs.

frog.speaker: H
frog.excerpt: We walked to Edremit. It was a three kilometre walk there. At the shops we bought bread and fruit. On the way back, we saw a dead squirrel. Dad and Francis found some frogs.

fred.speaker: F
fred.excerpt: We went to Zelve and parked Fred then we read til four. At four, we got out and started walking through a valley. There was a dried up river. We split up, the girls went along the riverbed. Me and Dad walked higher up in the rocks. Then Dad saw a church. It had a crack in the roof and two walls were missing. I found a pass into another valley. We went through and found that we could get in the church. Dad took a photo. We found a ladder leading to a dark room with a passage to a window at the end. Then I found another room with a tunnel to a window. It was about eighty feet down. Then we went back. It was amazing how much more our eyes could see. We then went back to the pass and went back to the river bed because there was a huge cave, only Dad, me and H went in. There were millions of tunnels and chimneys, rooms, and windows. We weren’t allowed much time. Then we got out and left.

fred.speaker: D
fred.excerpt: Lots of goats came, while we were eating breakfast, Helena and Francis were having theirs in the bivouac, and were soon surrounded, it was OK though. We drove to Lake Van, the people weren’t very friendly, and some boys threw stones at us, and hit. In a town, there was a fight, luckily, we weren’t in the middle of it. When at long last, we found a stop, (near a Police station) we were quickly surrounded by people, it was very difficult eating in front of them. We didn’t have enough though, for all all of them. In the end, Mum and F went and got the Police, the people went away, but we drove Fred to the station, just in case.

puncture_tyre_breakdown.speaker: G/M
puncture_tyre_breakdown.excerpt: Pergammon v.g. Punctured front left tyre. Ran out of gas.

puncture_tyre_breakdown.speaker: D
puncture_tyre_breakdown.excerpt: Last night we camped in some pine trees, and some Poles came and camped next to us, they only spoke German and Russian though. When we left in the morning we found that we had a flat tyre. F and I played Scrabble while Mum and Dad mended the wheel. In the afternoon we went to visit the Asklepion of Pergammon. It was a very old Hospital, situated there because of the springs, there was an old Library and Amphitheatre as well. A long tunnel ran underground with holes in the roof, patients used to have to run through the tunnel, while priests shouted down the holes “get well, get well”. We also climbed up to the Acropolis, it was on a very steep hill, then we came down to a town and ate out, everything covered with pepper though.

puncture_tyre_breakdown.speaker: F
puncture_tyre_breakdown.excerpt: On the way to Iran, we saw some small birds. They were like kingfishers and had very bright colours. We took some photos. Once when we stopped, someone thought that we had an accident but really we were taking a photo. Then we took some photos of eagles - they were huge. It was a very bumpy road. Suddenly we had a blowout - the tyre went bang and we stopped. Helena, Denise and I went to a river. H picked some perfect, posh, purple peppermints then we came back. Soon after we crossed the border and stopped in Iran.

puncture_tyre_breakdown.speaker: H
puncture_tyre_breakdown.excerpt: In the afternoon we had a blowout. While Dad changed the tyre, Denise, Francis and I went down to the river. I found lots of purple peppermint flowers.

camel.speaker: D
camel.excerpt: We drove into Bursa, and at length found the ‘Yesil’ (green) Mosque. We had to remove our shoes and Mum and I covered our heads. It was very beautiful, a nice man took us round, and up to the minaret, where tourists weren’t really allowed, it was all very old. Went to and old and new brass shop. I bought a little brass jar, we bargain all our things down. We also passed a caravanserai, where camel trains used to rest and sell etc.

camel.speaker: G/M
camel.excerpt: Spent night near Erdeck by sea. Lots of olives. Photo of Bird of Prey, Women in fields etc. Through v.large fields of sunflowers, maize etc. Also hills of purple heather and beehives. Saw 3 bears, muzzled walking alond road. Photo dancing bears. Saw ?? ?? ?? his house in 1357. Almost entirely hollow but still alive. Photo of camels etc near Troy. Stopped off a side road - 2 girls D & H’s age bought us ?? We gave them some peppers ?? ?? ??. Troy.

camel.speaker: D
camel.excerpt: Today we left the coast, and went inland. We saw some nomads, they had camels and donkeys, also horses and sheep. In the afternoon we went to see some underground cities, they were big places but lots of the passages we went through were small. It was very interesting. We had the guide who took ‘Blue Peter’ [UK kids program on BBC] round a few years ago.

stork.speaker: D
stork.excerpt: Last night, just out of Xanthis, we went down a road in between fields to camp, lots of peasant farmers passed us, there were lots of mosquitos. We are driving to Turkey and Istanbul, we are seeing lots of storks in big parties, and other migrating birds. When we reached Istanbul, we found our campsite, it is very nice and clean, it has hot water - free! We ate out in the camp restaurant. I had siskebab with chips, and lemonade. When we got back to the van we had a delicious melon, which we bought at a market.

stork.speaker: F
stork.excerpt: We woke up at 7 o’clock. Me and Helena went blackberry picking. I saw a spider about as big as a house spider - it had yellow and black horizontal stripes on its abdomen and legs, the head was a light grey. We saw a flock of migrating storks. We took some pictures of them. Denise and I stalked them!

stork.speaker: D
stork.excerpt: At the campsite we had a swim, in the rather shallow pool and then H and I had a shower, in the middle of which there was a blackout, it only lasted about 5 min. and then stopped. Mum and Dad told us about a stork that had fallen on to an electric wire and been electrocuted (killed, dead). That was probably the cause of the lights going out.

bazaar.speaker: G/M
bazaar.excerpt: Into Istanbul on Minibus. REAL experience - squashed, terrifying and friendly. Went to covered Bazaar. Saw coppersmiths, leather etc, some carpets. Girls bought onyx pillbox and pestle and mortar. Lunch just outside bazaar - good. Walked to Underground Cisterns - v. impressive. Then to Topkapi Palace - jewels were unbelievable. Pretty ??. Bought some ?? reserve.

bazaar.speaker: D
bazaar.excerpt: I hardly slept at all last night because of the mosquitoes. We are now going to see (Istanbul) the City. When at last we found the right Minibus, we only just squeezed in. When we got out, went and walked past some shops, we got lost, but finally made our way to the big covered bazaar. There were lots of leather coats and bags for sale. There were also shops selling onyx, I looked round and finally I found a pestle and mortar that I looked, the man said 100L as a specially low price, but we bargained down to 75L. I also tried on some coats and jackets, but I didn’t buy any. When we came out it was raining, and we went and had siskebab for lunch. We went to see the big underground cistern, it had 336 pillars, and it was an emergency water supply for the City, it is not used anymore and is only about 1 metre deep. It was about 1400 years old. When we finished we walked up to a big palace, it had belonged to a long succession of Sultans and was now a kind of museum, there were some magnificent plates and bowls etc and the jewel room was fantastic. There were some enormous jewels, emeralds in particular. Helena and I went on a guided tour of the Harem, it was enormous. We came out, lost ourselves (again) had a meal, and finally found ourselves back in the minibus place again. We found one going to the campsite and again squeezed ourselves on, we were even more squashed up, but it was unbelievable, we already had about 30 people, the bus just seated 20, and during the course of our journey, about 5 more somehow squashed in.

bazaar.speaker: F
bazaar.excerpt: We had breakfast and did our diaries then we got the 6 minibus. It was fast. The driver spoke in English to me. We stopped near the Bazaar, we went in, it was quite crowded. There were jewellers, copper, onyx and leather shops. Helena got a small oval box, gold with an onyx lid. Denise got an onyx pestle and mortar. Then we went to Topkapi Palace. It was made by the Turkish Sultans. In the Treasury there were two hugh identical candlesticks each with 6666 diamonds for the 6666 verses of the Koran and they weighed together 272000 grams!

bazaar.speaker: H
bazaar.excerpt: Today we took a minibus to Istanbul. We passed a bazaar then we went to a square. Daddy looked at the map, we were at the University. Afterwards, we walked to a covered bazaar. We passed lots of coats then we came to a shop which sold pillboxes. I saw one I liked. I bought it for 50 lira. It has gold walls with flowers printed on it, the stone in the lid is green with brown - it is called onyx. Went to a palace (Topkapi). Denise and I went on a guided tour of the Harem. The Harem is the place where the Sultan keeps his 400 or more wives. If his wives fall in love with anyone else, they get their heads chopped off.

mosque.speaker: D
mosque.excerpt: Today we went in to Istanbul in the van, and we visited some Mosques, the first was not very nice, but the second Mosque, the Blue Mosque was much nicer, and we had to take our shoes off, because the Muslims put their heads on the floor. After lunch we drove off and crossed the bridge into Asia.

mosque.speaker: F
mosque.excerpt: Went to the Blue Mosque. There were lots of tiles, mostly blue. The Moslims pray 5 times a day. In the mosque you are not allowed to wear shoes. The floor was one mass of carpets. We went to a park and had lunch.

mosque.speaker: H
mosque.excerpt: We have been to the Blue Mosque. It was nice. We had to take off our shoes before going inside. The muslims pray five times every day. The ceiling had pretty patterns. It’s called the Blue Mosque because the tiles on the walls are blue.

mosque.speaker: D
mosque.excerpt: We drove into Bursa, and at length found the ‘Yesil’ (green) Mosque. We had to remove our shoes and Mum and I covered our heads. It was very beautiful, a nice man took us round, and up to the minaret, where tourists weren’t really allowed, it was all very old. Went to and old and new brass shop. I bought a little brass jar, we bargain all our things down. We also passed a caravanserai, where camel trains used to rest and sell etc.

mosque.speaker: F
mosque.excerpt: Finished Bivouac and did diaries. We went to the council Mosque. We climbed a pinnacle - we were not meant to. Dad took a photo. It was once used by the Turkish government.

mosque.speaker: F
mosque.excerpt: The Green or Council mosque has libraries - each 400 years old. Some people were praying. The Sultan and a few of the harem used to be there.

mosque.speaker: H
mosque.excerpt: We have been to the Green Mosque. We went up the minaret where tourists are not allowed to go. Afterwards, we went shopping and got a red jewel, a pair of clogs and a necklace.

mosque.speaker: D
mosque.excerpt: We camped on a beach, right next to the sea, just out of Alanya. It was lovely and sandy, but when we got up at 1.00 at night to have a swim, we discovered that in the water, it was all rocky, there were some big breakers, we just stood in the waves. In the morning there were lorries everywhere, filing up with sand. We went back to Alanya to visit a castle, it was 800’ high on a mountain jutting out from the coastline, its outside walls were 5 miles long in all, it was really almost a little city, with 400 water cisterns, public baths and a mosque, it was restored in 13th century AD by the Seljuks.

onyx.excerpt: We left the Mocamp and drove to Ortahisar, in the middle of the small town was a big rock, that had been hollowed out into to passages and small rooms, we climbed to the top and had a super view of the surrounding countryside, and we could see lots of apricots etc drying on the roofs. When we came down we met a man who took us to his house to see some carpet making. He then invited us to stay the night at his house. We accepted and said that we’d come at about 6.00 that night. We drove off and went to visit Avanos. There, we visited onyx and pottery shops and saw men making things. I bought a little onyx goblet, and bargained down to 15tL (45p) from 20tL (60p). Then we went to a pottery shop. We saw a man making lots of cups. I bought a small one for 12p instead of 15p. Then we went to see more ‘rock ruins’ at Zelve. When we came back to the Turkish house, we sat round, drinking Chai and talking - or trying to. At last we got to bed, and although nice to sleep in a house the mattresses weren’t all that comfy.

onyx.speaker: H
onyx.excerpt: Then we went to a town and Denise bought something. It was the shape of an eggcup but it was very small and made of onyx.

carpet.speaker: H
carpet.excerpt: At Kaysery (sic), we visited a carpet shop. When we went in, the carpets were in rolls against the walls. The man who owned the shop got lots of carpets down but we did not want them. We liked three of them but did not buy one. They were all dyed with vegetable dyes, some of the carpets were wool or wool and cotton, and silk ones. The carpets are made with lots of knots, but Kelims are woven. I liked the silk carpets because they were so fine and shiny. I also liked the wool ones because they are so soft.

melon.speaker: D
melon.excerpt: We camped near the sea, but didn’t swim. Drove along and when we stopped for lunch, a nice girl came and gave us two melons, she had her younger sister with her, they gave us some more things, and we gave them some sweets. We drove on and found a nice view across the sea to Europe, and asked the way to Troy, we received directions and went on our way. When we arrived, almost the first thing we saw was an enormous wooden horse, we were able to climb up into it, like the Greeks. We went all round the old walls, a lot was left to the imagination though. There were 9 layers of the city, the earliest dating from about 3000 BC.

goat.speaker: D
goat.excerpt: We’ve seen lots of goats round our campsite. Went to Antalya, it was very hot. We had a drink overlooking the harbour, and then some delicious ice cream. We then drove on to Lara beach where we swam. Then we drove to see the Aspendos Amphitheatre, it looked like a big house, perhaps 200 years old from the front, but inside was a big sweep of seats around a stage, the acoustics were superb.

goat.excerpt: Lots of goats came, while we were eating breakfast, Helena and Francis were having theirs in the bivouac, and were soon surrounded, it was OK though. underground_city.speaker: F
underground_city.excerpt: We went to an underground city. It was very cold. They used millstones to shut the door. It was used as a hideout. You could even keep animals in there.

underground_city.speaker: H
underground_city.excerpt: We have been to an underground city. There were lots of very small passages. There were also some big millstones which were used to stop enemies getting in. We were guided round by a nice guide who had 7 children and had guided the people from blue peter round. (Pic)

chai.speaker: H
chai.excerpt: In the evening, we went to a Turkish man’s house. We were all given some chai. They had a big flat roof where they were drying lots of onions and apricots. There were also some unshelled almonds there - and found that if you smash the pip of an apricot there is a kernel in it.

chai.speaker: D
chai.excerpt: We went into Van itself, and had lunch in a Restaurant that a man in the tourist information recommended to us. It was very nice, the first place where everyone liked the food. Then we went to the museum, it had lots of different and old writing. (diagram here). Then we went down to the sea where there was a great outcrop of rock with the ruins of an old castle on it. I finished the film of the camera, taking a shot of Mum and a tower. The castle was basically stone with mud bricks on top, the mud had kept very well, for over 2000 years. We went back into Van, and bought a new film for the camera. Then we went to a Jandarma place, there was a beach, we swam, but it was very cold. We had chai with the soldiers, and played ‘Liar dice’. [Jandarma is a Turkish Police Station where you can camp.]
